title: MDX's missing-component error is a diagnostic, not a boundary
statement: MDX requires a referenced component to be defined and fails at RUNTIME when it is not, with the message `Expected component X to be defined: you likely forgot to import, pass, or provide it`. The failure occurs when a reference resolves to nothing; a document that imports a component, defines one locally, or is passed one never reaches it. The check therefore reports an authoring mistake and does not constrain what a document may reference or execute.
notes: ⚠️ THIS IS THE CANDIDATE ANSWER TO QST-0018'S THIRD PART, AND IT DOES NOT SURVIVE. The question asked what happens to a reference outside the permitted set — refuse, or render inert. MDX refuses, which sounds like the answer the question wanted. It is not: it refuses references to components that were never supplied, which is the case a mistaken author hits and not the case a capable one does. A document that reaches for something it should not have can simply import it, and then it IS defined. ⚠️ AND THE REFUSAL IS AT RUNTIME. Even used as a diagnostic, it surfaces when a page is rendered rather than when the document is written or the project is built — so a stage document with a bad reference is a page that throws for the operator, not a build that refuses. ⚠️ Same shape as AST-0022, one layer up: a mechanism that looks like enforcement because it produces an error, while the case it catches is not the case that matters.
